also: I don’t mind if you stay
if it’s all right with you

evidence: Catull. 55.1: sī forte nōn molestum est
Cic. Clu. 168: tū autem, nisi molestum est, paulisper exsurge
Traupman 103: sī tibi molestum nōn est
terms.comment: With a dative of the person. Nisi molestum est or sī nōn molestum est: if you don’t mind.

evidence: Traupman 103: istuc quidem nōn molestē ferō
terms.comment: Nōn molestē ferō: I don’t mind.

terms.gloss: I don’t mind, I have no objection
evidence: Ter. Eun. 459: Ubi vīs, nōn moror.
Ant. in Cic. Phil. 13.35: nihil moror eōs salvōs esse

terms.gloss: if you don’t mind, if it’s all right with you
evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.7: sī tibi vidētur
Traupman 103: if you don’t mind, sī tibi vidētur
Traupman 105: if it’s O.K. with you, sī tibi vidētur
terms.comment: Literally “if it seems good to you”: the polite way to ask leave or to propose something (see suggest).

phrases.latin: ōrāmus, sī forte nōn molestum est, dēmōnstrēs ubi sint tuae tenebrae
phrases.english: Please, if you don’t mind, show us where your hiding place is.
Whenever you like; I’ve no objection.

phrases.latin: Nōn labōrō sī manēs, modo taceās.
phrases.english: I don’t mind if you stay, as long as you’re quiet.

sources: Lewis & Short: molestus · Lewis & Short: moror
